queue_items.claim: The row's opening seam at 2:17|2:18 rests on no ruled tier-1 signal in its own cited verse's bytes, and no tier-3 mark stands there either; the warrant is topical shift alone.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale grounds the open on 'a fresh topical turn after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17'; strongest_rejected_alternative confirms it: 'the unit is bounded instead by topical shift (from proud objects to idols and human flight) and the petuchah break closing the chapter.' The cited verse is three tokens in full — “וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף” (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier) — a waw-conjunctive definite noun carrying no frame onset of any ruled class (no hoy, hinneh, koh-amar, neum, massa header, imperative, vocative or temporal formula), and the waw binds it to what precedes. The staged parashah inventory records NO mark at Isa.2.17 or Isa.2.18, so no tier-3 corroboration stands at this seam (absence is not counterevidence, but it leaves the seam unsupported). The row's own observed_substrate_signals — oracle_frame.concluding_summary and parashah.pe_boundary — both attach to the row's CLOSE at 2:22; the row records no opening-seam signal at all. Three further byte facts argue continuity across this seam: the verse-initial temporal formula “בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙” stands at oshb:Isa.2.20 (tokens 1-2, byte tier) INSIDE the span, so the only verse-initial temporal-formula onset in the neighbourhood is two verses past the chosen seam and the row mentions it merely as a recurring 'tag'; the flight-from-terror device the row itself discloses runs from oshb:Isa.2.10 (outside, in the 2:5-11 stanza) into oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (inside), its four-token core “מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר” collating byte at oshb:Isa.2.10 and accent_stripped at the two later sites (sweep: 3 verses, accent_stripped); and frontier_flag_considered is false on the weakest-warranted row in this batch.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY — route the 2:17|2:18 seam to adjudication with three options recorded: (a) respan to fold this material into the preceding refrain-closed stanza, M8-Isa-011 Isa.2.12-Isa.2.17 becoming Isa.2.12-Isa.2.22 as a one-edit seam-pair cure; (b) re-cut this row to Isa.2.20-Isa.2.22 on the verse-initial temporal formula at oshb:Isa.2.20 (byte tier), leaving 2:18-19 with the preceding stanza; (c) retain Isa.2.18-Isa.2.22 but set frontier_flag_considered true, lower confidence, and disclose the tier-1 shortfall at the opening seam. Any replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original.

queue_items.claim: A tier-3 single-witness petuchah is named as one of the two grounds that bound the unit, while the genuine tier-1 signal at that seam is never cited.
queue_items.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative: 'the unit is bounded instead by topical shift ... and the petuchah break closing the chapter'; observed_substrate_signals carries parashah.pe_boundary. The mark checks out — the staged parashah inventory records Isa.2.22 as PE, and boundary_rationale discloses it correctly as single-witness, tier-3 — but in the Prophets the layer never bounds a unit. The tier-1 signal at this rear seam stands in the next verse's bytes, “כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת” (oshb:Isa.3.1, tokens 1-5, byte tier), which the neighbour row M8-Isa-013 argues as its hinneh-announcement onset and which this row neither quotes nor lists in boundary_evidence_refs.
queue_items.proposed_change: Re-ground the rear warrant on the hinneh-announcement onset at oshb:Isa.3.1, add that ref to boundary_evidence_refs, demote the Isa.2.22 petuchah to disclosed corroboration, and rename the oss key to parashah.pe_corroboration.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier), “The idols shall utterly pass away.” (web:Isa.2.18), moving from the refrain-closed catalogue of proud things to the idols' own fate and humanity's flight into caves and holes, a fresh topical turn after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17. The row runs through the closing exhortation “Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?” (oshb:Isa.2.22), where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.22, single-witness, tier-3) at the chapter's end.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:18-22 as a third refrain-bounded stanza of the same shape as 2:5-11 and 2:12-17 was rejected because no closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause recurs at its end; the unit is bounded instead by topical shift (from proud objects to idols and human flight) and the petuchah break closing the chapter.

shipped_row.device_notes: The ‘in that day’ temporal tag recurs at verse 20 (web:Isa.2.20), continuing the temporal frame of the refrain-closed stanzas without reopening the refrain clause itself. A flight-from-terror motif straddles the row's own opening seam: the four-token core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר recurs at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 within this row, with a third site further upstream at oshb:Isa.2.10, accent_stripped tier across the three (sweep: 3 verses). Within the row, the two in-span sites share a longer eight-token run, מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, byte-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte).

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the Day-of-Yahweh formula כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.2.12, byte tier), “For there will be a day of Yahweh of Armies” (web:Isa.2.12), a fresh temporal-formula onset launching the catalogue of high and lofty things (cedars, oaks, mountains, towers, ships, imagery) that closes on the same refrain clause as the preceding stanza, וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא (oshb:Isa.2.17, byte tier), “Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day.” (web:Isa.2.17). Verse 11, right before this row starts, is itself setumah-marked (oshb:Isa.2.11, single-witness, tier-3), the same mark disclosed as the closing witness for the stanza it ends.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the high-things catalogue (2:13-16) from its opening formula (2:12) and closing refrain (2:17) into separate rows was rejected because the catalogue is a single polysyndetic (waw-coordinated) list: the preposition עַ֥ל/וְעַ֖ל governing the quantifier כָּל as its object recurs eight times across 2:13-16, matching the governing verse's own two-part coordination at oshb:Isa.2.12 (עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם without the conjunction, וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל with it), not a self-standing unit, read here as enumeration inside its governing oracle rather than a separate row.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The cedar/oak/mountain/tower/ship catalogue (2:13-16) is enumeration inside this unit, not an independent list register; polysyndetic (waw-coordinated) inventory catalogues of this kind are read as texture inside their governing oracle here, not as a unit on its own. The row's own opening seam carries cross-seam cohesion: oshb:Isa.2.12 opens with כִּ֣י (oshb:Isa.2.12), the same particle that opens oshb:Isa.2.6 inside the preceding stanza's own span (web:Isa.2.5-Isa.2.11), both witnesses rendering it as subordinating there. The low/bow root runs unbroken across the seam and through the stanza — וַיִּשְׁפַּל (oshb:Isa.2.9), שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11), וְשָׁפֵֽל (oshb:Isa.2.12) — standing at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton), and it interleaves at 2:12-14 with the paired high/lofty vocabulary that the row's own catalogue enumerates (הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.13, הָרָמִ֑ים / הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.2.14), closing again with וְשַׁח֙ גַּבְה֣וּת הָאָדָ֔ם וְשָׁפֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.2.17. That link leaves a live rival unstated: one sustained pride-and-humbling poem running from 2:9 through 2:17, with the refrain as internal punctuation rather than a row-cutting seam.

The row runs through the causal explanation and the gnomic gender-reversal saying, closing on “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them” (oshb:Isa.3.12), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.3.12, single-witness, tier-3), before the fresh riv/din legal formula of verse 13.

next_row.device_notes: Verses 9 and 11 each carry the interjection א֣וֹי / א֖וֹי (oshb:Isa.3.9 token 10; oshb:Isa.3.11 token 1, byte tier at each site), a lexeme distinct from the hoy ה֣וֹי of oshb:Isa.1.4 and 1:24 and not blended with it here (the hoy-onset lexeme stands at 22 verses book-wide, sweep: 22 verses, skeleton); the interjection itself is a 4-verse token-exact object (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton, token-exact), while a bare three-letter substring sweep returns 8 verses, the extra 4 being contained-consonant hits inside unrelated words elsewhere in the book — these sites are read as gnomic-retribution texture inside the unit, not as fresh hoy-onset seams.

queue_items.claim: The 22-verse hoy digit is labelled as the onset object, but it is the token-verse object and it includes a verse whose token is a different lexeme.
queue_items.grounds: device_notes: '(the hoy-onset lexeme stands at 22 verses book-wide, sweep: 22 verses, skeleton)'. Re-swept from the pointed form spliced at oshb:Isa.5.20 token 1, “ה֣וֹי”: skeleton 22 verses / accent_stripped 21 / byte 5. The staged device inventory carries the same split — 22 token-verses against 20 verse-initial — under an explicit role-split-before-counting note separating woe-oracle onsets from the 1:4 indictment, the 1:24 self-exclamation and the 55:1 invitation; by that role split the woe-oracle onset subclass is 18, not 22. The skeleton 22 also carries Isa.16.4, whose token is “מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי סֵ֥תֶר” (oshb:Isa.16.4, tokens 4-6, byte tier) — an imperative of the be-verb, not the hoy lexeme. So the named object matches neither the counted object nor the onset subclass. The same sentence's oy work is by contrast exact and is confirmed on re-sweep: token-exact skeleton 4 verses (Isa.3.9, 3.11, 6.5, 24.16) against a bare three-letter substring 8 verses, the extra 4 being Isa.1.24, 26.9, 35.8 and 63.10.
queue_items.proposed_change: Restate as the token object with its scope and role given — e.g. 22 token-verses book-wide of which 20 are verse-initial — applying to hoy the same object discipline this sentence already applies to oy.

next_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the explicit legal-summons formula נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים (oshb:Isa.3.13, byte tier), “Yahweh stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.” (web:Isa.3.13), the contend-infinitive לָרִ֖יב (token 2) standing at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact) and the judge-infinitive לָדִ֥ין (token 5) at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton, token-exact), so the pairing cannot recur anywhere else in the book, addressed to “the elders of his people and their leaders” (web:Isa.3.14), a distinct addressee from the general my-people material of the preceding unit. The row closes on the postpositive signature נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.3.15, byte tier), “says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.” (oshb:Isa.3.15), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.3.15, single-witness, tier-3; the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note not engaged by this quoted signature clause), before the fresh vayomer narrative onset of verse 16. This same opening seam has its own tier-3 witness: a setumah break closes verse 12 (oshb:Isa.3.12, single-witness) immediately before the row begins.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row into the preceding leadership-collapse unit (3:1-12) was rejected because verse 13 opens with its own verse-initial legal-summons formula, נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים (oshb:Isa.3.13, byte tier), addressed to a distinct addressee (the elders and leaders) rather than continuing the general my-people material. Running the row on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16 was also rejected, since that verse opens its own וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה narrative formula (the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note later in its own line, not engaged by this quoted onset), a distinct frame class from the postpositive neum signature closing this row at verse 15.

queue_items.claim: The row's nominated rear-seam warrant - that MT 7:18 opens an oracle cycle which "names no speaker and addresses no one directly" - does not survive the bytes of the cycle it characterises, and it is the warrant the row expressly prefers over the day-formula.
queue_items.grounds: The row demotes the only formal signal at the seam ("The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself") and rests the seam on the frame-mode characterisation instead, so that characterisation is load-bearing. MT 7:25, inside the characterised cycle, carries "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier), which the row's own second witness renders as a direct second-person address, “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) - a verse inside the range this row lists at web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25. The identical warrant sentence is carried at the facing row for web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25, where it stands two sentences from that row's own contrary statement that the cycle is "addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative" and from its rejected-alternative ground that "the four share one addressee". Honest limit: no morphology layer is available in the staged extract, so the person of "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier) cannot be machine-settled from the pointed bytes alone (2ms and 3fs are both open); that ambiguity is itself a reason the characterisation cannot carry a seam, and the in-field contradiction stands regardless of how the form is parsed.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: delete the "names no speaker and addresses no one directly" clause and re-argue the rear seam from byte facts actually at the seam - the close of the named-participant narrative scene at MT 7:17 and the verse-initial oracle-frame onset "{718_ext}" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) - with the tier-3 petuchah at oshb:Isa.7.17 kept as disclosed corroboration only. No span change proposed.

queue_items.claim: "Four verse-initial speech onsets punctuate the span" is a digit whose swept object is unnamed and which is short for the object as stated.
queue_items.grounds: MT 7:12, inside the span, opens verse-initially on "וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז" (oshb:Isa.7.12, byte tier) - a fifth verse-initial speech onset, unnamed by the row; MT 7:2 likewise opens on the report formula "וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר" (oshb:Isa.7.2, byte tier). The four the row does name (oshb:Isa.7.3, oshb:Isa.7.7, oshb:Isa.7.10, oshb:Isa.7.13) are the divine/prophetic frame onsets, but the row counts the unqualified class "verse-initial speech onsets", and the campaign's frame-owner count discipline requires the object be named before the digit. The digit is not alone load-bearing: MT 7:12's reply sits inside the same third-person frame and does not reopen the row.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: name the object (e.g. "four verse-initial divine-frame speech onsets") or restate the digit to include MT 7:12. No span change.

queue_items.claim: The rejected alternative is set aside on the ground that "no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the sign speech from the surrounding narrative scene", but the row's own splices place a ruled tier-1 vocative-imperative onset immediately before the sign speech.
queue_items.grounds: The row itself splices "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier) - a verse-initial speech formula plus imperative plus vocative - and the addressee shifts across it from the 2ms address to Ahaz, "שְׁאַל לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת" (oshb:Isa.7.11, byte tier), to the 2mp of the house of David, "הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier). Vocative and imperative onsets explicit in the bytes are ruled tier-1 in this book's frame spine, so the blanket ground as written is contradicted by the row's own cited evidence. The span itself is defensible under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule; only the stated ground fails.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A third-person narrative frame opens the row: "וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ" (oshb:Isa.7.1, byte tier), matching “In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.” (web:Isa.7.1) -- a clean scene shift from the throne-vision report. Four verse-initial speech onsets punctuate the span without reopening it: "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒" (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), matching “Then Yahweh said to Isaiah” (web:Isa.7.3); "כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.7.7, byte tier), matching “This is what the Lord Yahweh says” (web:Isa.7.7); "וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Isa.7.10, byte tier), matching “Yahweh spoke again to Ahaz, saying,” (web:Isa.7.10); and "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier), matching “Listen now, house of David” (web:Isa.7.13). These four stand inside the third-person narrative frame opened at web:Isa.7.1 rather than beside it, so the frame owns the embedded speech and nothing among the four reopens the row; the same narrative frame does not extend past its own close, which is why its defective-spelled resumptive twin at oshb:Isa.8.5 opens a fresh row rather than continuing this one. The frame runs through the Immanuel sign to its closing threat, “Yahweh will bring on you, on your people, and on your father’s house days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria.” (web:Isa.7.17), where the next verse’s repeated “in that day” formula (web:Isa.7.18) opens a different oracle cycle. The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself: the narrated direct-address scene that has framed the intervening speech since web:Isa.7.1 gives way here to an impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly.

HELD, NEVER DECIDED: the sign’s referent term, "הָעַלְמָ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.7.14, byte tier), matching “the virgin” (web:Isa.7.14), and the Immanuel formation that follows it, "עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל" (oshb:Isa.7.14, byte tier), matching “Immanuel” (web:Isa.7.14) -- the first of the book’s three עמנו אל sites (sweep: 3 verses) -- carry the book’s classic construal crux; this row holds the sign’s meaning open rather than deciding it, per standing governance. prev_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh first-person vision report opens the row on a date-frame clause, not one of the book’s three vision-superscription headers: "בִּשְׁנַת מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה אֶת אֲדֹנָ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל כִּסֵּ֖א רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֑א וְשׁוּלָ֖יו מְלֵאִ֥ים אֶת הַהֵיכָֽל" (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte tier), matching “In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.” (web:Isa.6.1) -- a scene shift unrelated to the preceding invasion imagery. The report runs through the commissioning exchange and the hardening oracle to its stump-remnant close, “If there is a tenth left in it, that also will in turn be consumed, as a terebinth, and as an oak whose stump remains when they are cut down, so the holy seed is its stump.” (web:Isa.6.13), where the following chapter opens a third-person narrative scene (web:Isa.7.1) under a wholly different frame. Because this row's span runs the whole of chapter 6 start to finish (13 verses, per the book's verse inventory), its confidence sits at the medium_low ceiling the campaign sets for any whole-chapter unit, not at a lower band earned by a fresh defect.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative splits the commissioning exchange (web:Isa.6.8-Isa.6.10) from the throne vision as a separate call-narrative row, but the first-person report frame runs without a break from web:Isa.6.1 through the stump image, arguing one vision-report unit.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on the first of four repeated “in that day” formulas structuring the unit: "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ לַזְּב֔וּב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה יְאֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלַ֨דְּבוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אַשּֽׁוּר" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier), matching “It will happen in that day that Yahweh will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.” (web:Isa.7.18). Its extended opener, "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier), is accent-stripped-identical to the extended opener of web:Isa.7.21, "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.21, byte tier), and of web:Isa.7.23, though the three are not byte-identical to one another (sweep: 13 verses book-wide at the extended, accent-stripped form; 45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form). web:Isa.7.20 opens on the shorter "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) without the leading element and is a different attested form, disclosed rather than counted with the other three. The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself: the narrated direct-address scene that has framed the intervening speech since web:Isa.7.1 gives way here to an impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly. These four images bind the fly/bee, razor, and briers-and-thorns pictures into one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative but marked off from it by their own repeated formula rather than a fresh scene. The cycle runs to “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.” (web:Isa.7.25), where chapter 8’s sign-act command (web:Isa.8.1) opens a new divine-command frame.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative atomizes the row into four separate rows, one per 'in that day' onset (web:Isa.7.18, web:Isa.7.20, web:Isa.7.21, web:Isa.7.23), but the four share one addressee and one cumulative judgment image, lacking any addressee shift or divine-frame renewal between them, arguing one coherent oracle unit under the over-split-risk rule.

queue_items.claim: The row's nominated front-seam warrant - an "impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly" - is contradicted twice inside the row's own boundary_rationale and by the bytes of the row's own closing verse.
queue_items.grounds: The same field states the seam "is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence ... but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself", making the characterisation load-bearing; two sentences later the same field calls the unit "one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative", and the rejected alternative adds that "the four share one addressee ... lacking any addressee shift". The row's own closing verbatim WEB quotation carries the direct address it denies: “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.” (web:Isa.7.25), against MT bytes "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier). Honest limit: with no morphology layer staged, the person of "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier) is not machine-settleable from the pointed bytes (2ms and 3fs both open) - which is itself a reason the characterisation cannot carry a seam; the in-field self-contradiction stands independently of the parse.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: delete the "addresses no one directly" clause; re-argue the front seam from the verse-initial oracle-frame onset "{718_ext}" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) taken together with the close of the named-participant narrative scene at MT 7:17, and reconsider confidence (currently medium with frontier_flag_considered false) once the warrant is restated. No span change proposed.

queue_items.claim: The "45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form" digit carries no tier label and is wrong under the only tier named in its own parenthetical.
queue_items.grounds: The parenthetical reads "(sweep: 13 verses book-wide at the extended, accent-stripped form; 45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form)". Re-swept as verse counts from the staged text: the extended opener "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) gives 13 verses at accent-stripped tier - the row's first digit re-verifies exactly. The bare form "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) gives 41 verses at accent-stripped tier (that tier retains meteg, which separates MT 2:11, 2:17, 3:7, 29:18), 45 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier, and 12 verses at byte tier. The shipped 45 is therefore a skeleton-tier count presented with no tier of its own inside a parenthetical whose only named tier is accent-stripped, where the correct digit is 41. Not alone load-bearing: the row expressly declines to argue the seam from this recurrence.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: label the digit's tier - "45 verses book-wide at the bare form, consonantal-skeleton tier" - or restate as "41 verses ... accent-stripped". No span change.
